items.text: Eat a handful of walnuts.
items.why: They contain arginine and plant omega-3; they support blood vessel health.

source.title: Esposito et al. (2006) – Mediterranean diet and erectile function

items.text: Eat a handful of unsalted pistachios.
items.why: Rich in arginine and antioxidants.

items.text: Eat a handful of raw almonds.
items.why: A source of magnesium and vitamin E.

items.text: Add 1 tablespoon of pumpkin seeds to your yoghurt or salad.
items.why: One of the good sources of zinc, which is needed to produce testosterone.

items.text: Eat 1–2 squares of 70%+ cocoa dark chocolate.
items.why: Cocoa flavanols support the function of the inner lining of blood vessels.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat 1 Brazil nut; no more.
items.why: A single one covers your daily selenium need; selenium is important for reproductive health.

items.text: Eat a handful of cashews.
items.why: They contain zinc and magnesium.

items.text: Eat a handful of unsalted sunflower seeds.
items.why: A source of vitamin E and zinc.

items.text: Eat a handful of roasted chickpeas as a snack.
items.why: They provide plant protein, arginine and folate.

items.text: Add 1 teaspoon of ground flaxseed to your yoghurt.
items.why: Contains plant omega-3 and fibre.

items.text: Add 1 teaspoon of chia seeds to your yoghurt or milk.
items.why: Contains omega-3, fibre and magnesium.

items.text: Add 1 teaspoon of unsweetened cocoa to your milk.
items.why: Pure cocoa is one of the richest sources of flavanols.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Drink 1–2 cups of green tea.
items.why: Rich in flavonoids called catechins.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a bowl of blueberries.
items.why: Fruits rich in anthocyanins have been linked to a lower risk of erection problems.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a bowl of strawberries.
items.why: Strawberries were among the fruits that contributed most in the flavonoid research.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat half a pomegranate.
items.why: Rich in polyphenols; supports blood vessel health.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a few slices of watermelon; out of season, swap it for a bowl of strawberries.
items.why: Contains citrulline, which the body turns into arginine.

items.text: Eat an orange.
items.why: Citrus flavanones have been linked to a lower risk of erection problems.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat an apple.
items.why: Apples were among the fruits that stood out in the flavonoid research.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a banana.
items.why: Potassium and magnesium help keep blood pressure balanced.

items.text: Eat a handful of red or black grapes.
items.why: Their skins contain anthocyanins and resveratrol.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a bowl of cherries or sour cherries; out of season, a handful of dried ones.
items.why: Rich in anthocyanins.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a handful of blackberries or mulberries.
items.why: A source of anthocyanins and fibre.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat half an avocado.
items.why: Contains healthy fats, folate and magnesium.

items.text: Eat two mandarins.
items.why: A source of flavanones and vitamin C.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a pear.
items.why: Pears, along with apples, were among the fruits that stood out in the flavonoid research.

source.title: Cassidy et al. (2016) – Flavonoid intake and erectile dysfunction, AJCN

items.text: Eat a kiwi.
items.why: One covers most of your daily vitamin C need.

items.text: Add beetroot to your meal.
items.why: Contains natural nitrate; nitrate turns into nitric oxide, which relaxes blood vessels.

source.title: Beetroot nitrate and blood pressure – meta-analysis (2022)

items.text: Add a handful of rocket to your salad.
items.why: One of the greens richest in nitrate.

source.title: Inorganic nitrate and cardiovascular risk factors – meta-analysis (2018)

items.text: Add spinach to one of your meals.
items.why: A source of nitrate, folate and magnesium.

source.title: Inorganic nitrate and cardiovascular risk factors – meta-analysis (2018)

items.text: Eat a portion of broccoli.
items.why: Contains folate and vitamin C.

items.text: Eat tomatoes with one meal.
items.why: Contains lycopene; a staple of Mediterranean-style eating.

source.title: Esposito et al. (2006) – Mediterranean diet and erectile function

items.text: Add a spoonful of olive oil to your salad.
items.why: In one study, an olive-oil-based Mediterranean diet improved erectile function.

source.title: Esposito et al. (2006) – Mediterranean diet and erectile function

items.text: Eat eggs at breakfast.
items.why: Provide vitamin D, B12 and high-quality protein.

items.text: Eat salmon or mackerel with one meal.
items.why: A source of omega-3 and vitamin D.

items.text: Eat anchovies or sardines with one meal.
items.why: Affordable fish rich in omega-3.

items.text: Eat chickpeas with one meal.
items.why: Contain arginine, zinc and folate.

items.text: Have a bowl of lentil soup.
items.why: Provides folate, zinc and plant protein.

items.text: Eat turkey or chicken breast with one meal.
items.why: A source of arginine and zinc.

items.text: Eat mussels or prawns with one meal.
items.why: Shellfish are among the richest sources of zinc.
